name: Yanji DPRK IT-workforce and host-employer context (2015)

attribution.legal_posture: The source presents the activity as supported employment and industrial policy; cited material covers legitimate development, training, and cooperation context. Fraud, criminal case, sanctions action, labor violation, and immigration enforcement require separate evidence.

statements: Yanji High-Tech Zone reported that it coordinated with the DPRK consulate and DPRK companies concerning the quantity and quality of DPRK IT recruitment.
The report stated that 14 companies in the zone employed DPRK IT technical personnel and that 312 personnel had been introduced cumulatively during the reported period.
The employers and workers are unnamed; the aggregate historical count does not identify any front company, facilitator, persona, account, or individual worker.
Original-language evidence: “高新区积极协调朝鲜领事馆和朝鲜会社，保证朝鲜IT人才引进的数量和质量，全区招用朝鲜IT技术人才企业达到14家，累计引进朝鲜IT技术人才312人。”

Researcher-supplied English translation: The report said the high-tech zone coordinated with the DPRK consulate and DPRK companies to maintain the quantity and quality of DPRK IT recruitment; 14 companies in the zone employed DPRK IT technical personnel, with 312 personnel introduced cumulatively.
infrastructure.evidence_class: historical official Chinese employment and industrial-development statement
infrastructure.translation_method: Close researcher translation of the reviewed Simplified Chinese official text.
limitations: Do not identify the 14 employers through registry correlation or assume they were fronts.
Do not treat the historical count as current as of 2026.
Do not infer a fraudulent-employment nexus for any individual worker from nationality or location alone.
Do not identify the 14 employers through registry correlation, geography, later reporting, or name similarity, and do not characterize them as fronts.
The two local companies named elsewhere in the source are not linked by the text to the aggregate workforce count and are not represented here.
The 312 unnamed workers must not be resolved or attributed through nationality, location, names, images, social graphs, or later sanctions reporting.
This is historical workforce and organizational context, not proof of fraudulent employment, deception, sanctions evasion, misconduct, or a current operation.
No named person, facilitator, persona, account, prosecution, front company, sensitive identifier, address, payment selector, identity document, or image is retained.
